subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime callers be categorically denied from patching legacy ownerless session rows, with operators or non-plugin clients as the recovery path?
rationale: No stored owner exists from which plugin authority can be derived safely, but enforcing that rule can intentionally break legacy plugin workflows and therefore requires explicit ownership and upgrade-policy approval.

options.title: Approve Fail-Closed Boundary
options.body: Accept exact owner equality, land this proven patch, and require the sibling sessions.create work to reuse the same canonical invariant.

options.title: Add Explicit Ownership Migration
options.body: Delay landing until a narrow operator-controlled migration or claim workflow is designed for legitimate legacy ownerless rows.

options.title: Pause For Sibling Consolidation
options.body: Hold this PR until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103148 establishes the shared ownership helper and then rebase this fix onto it.

recommendation.title: Approve Fail-Closed Boundary
recommendation.body: Accept exact owner equality, land this proven patch, and require the sibling sessions.create work to reuse the same canonical invariant.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session-lifecycle and persistence work makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the cross-path ownership decision.
